decisive_question.question: Is the slowdown in Contract Value and revenue a cyclical air-pocket driven by exogenous federal/tariff/funding shocks that normalise, or the onset of a durable structural growth stall in the core Insights subscription engine?

evidence_for.claim: Management attributes the slowdown to specific external forces (DOGE, tariffs, state/local funding, non-AI tech) and reports CV grew ~4% ex-US-federal, framing the weakness as exogenous and concentrated.
evidence_for.source_ref: CIQ transcript(s): Gartner, Inc., Q1 2026 Earnings Call, May 05, 2026.rtf; Gartner, Inc., Q4 2025 Earnings Call, Feb 03, 2026.rtf

evidence_for.claim: Insights is 78% of revenue (5,073 of 6,497) and is described as subscription-based with strong retention and FCF in excess of net income, a base that can re-accelerate if the shocks fade.

evidence_against.claim: Same-quarter revenue is already negative at -1.5% YoY and EBITDA margin has fallen four consecutive years (24%→20%), consistent with a structural rather than one-off deterioration.
evidence_against.source_ref: CIQ Financials→Income Statement + Segments + Ratios (multi-year columns)

evidence_against.claim: Revenue revisions are 0↑/3↓ and consensus sits at Hold (3.00), indicating analysts do not yet treat the slowdown as a transient air-pocket.

key_unknowns: Revised forward guidance is UNKNOWN — no revised-outlook 99.1 exhibit was parsed for the 2026-02-03 8-K despite it being an earnings filing; absence of a forward guide on the gap-down event is a bearish opacity risk.
Adjusted EPS, forward adjusted EV/EBITDA, and adjusted net-debt/EBITDA are all UNKNOWN (not in the revised guidance), so the forward valuation basis used by management cannot be reconciled.
FCF sign is UNKNOWN (no OCF/capex breakout) — survival_capacity flags runway as not assessable, a bearish gap even though net-debt/EBITDA is 1.3x and nearest maturity wall is 2028.
Segment-level EBITDA is UNKNOWN (no EBITDA section on the Segments sheet), so the profitability of the 78% Insights segment versus Conferences/Consulting cannot be isolated.
No idiosyncratic-vs-shared cohort is available (IT absent from graph coverage), so the -68.3% relative move cannot be benchmarked against a peer cross-section.

Peer set is explicitly HETEROGENEOUS ($751M–$119.1B span, 159x); every peer multiple is a confidence-gated input, not a clean benchmark, and the EARNED-vs-RESIDUAL split of the discount is left for the human.
